qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Owns iconic Italian aperitif brands (Aperol, Campari) with proprietary recipes and cultural Lindy cachet. However, fails Gate 3b proof of moat: 5-year and 10-year median GAAP ROIC has structurally hovered at 7-8%, well below the 12% hurdle, diluted by goodwill-heavy acquisitions (Grand Marnier, €1.2B Courvoisier buyout) and high A&P spend required to maintain Aperol spritz momentum against cocktail fashion shifts.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing, REJECT). While Aperol and Campari possess strong cultural brand cachet, Campari fails Gate 3b with 5-year and 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 7-8%, failing the 12% hurdle. Returns diluted by expensive debt-funded M&A (Courvoisier) and high marketing reinvestment. Does not qualify for Calamity Tier as sub-12% ROIC is structural across the multi-year cycle.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~7.8%, with recent ROIC compressing toward ~5.4-6.1%. Net debt rose to €2.28B post the €1.2B Courvoisier acquisition, pushing net leverage to ~3.5x-3.9x EBITDA. Consecutive CEO transitions in 2024 (Bob Kunze-Concewitz stepping down, followed by Matteo Fantacchiotti abruptly exiting after 5 months) further eroded capital allocation consistency.
